name: Percival 'Percy' Ainsworth
equipment: .32 pocket pistol, mother-of-pearl grips, 8 rounds loaded, in a dinner jacket pocket cut for it
Straight razor, his grandfather's, silver-handled, in a waistcoat pocket
Rolodex of four hundred names, in a calfskin case, every one annotated in green ink with what they want
Three good suits and a white dinner jacket, all slightly too old
Gold cigarette case, engraved 'P. from Mother, 1935', containing Turkish cigarettes and a pawn ticket for the matching lighter
Club Sirocco card markers to the value of $3,000, in Royce Ambler's safe, not his pocket
Business cards: AINSWORTH & LOWE ARTISTS' REPRESENTATIVES - SUNSET BOULEVARD (Mr. Lowe died in 1944; Percy kept the name for tone)
features: Doors Open (Old Money origin: +2 Charisma, +1 Intelligence. Doormen, maîtres d' and private secretaries let him through unless told not to, and he has advantage on Society checks among the wealthy; below the tracks he has disadvantage on Streetwise until he has shown he can be trusted)

Favors Owed (a pool of 4 favours, refilled at the start of each case or after a week of downtime; one favour buys a name, a dropped charge, a car or a doctor who doesn't ask, a meeting, a file for an hour, or a warning before a raid; two buy something big. Every favour spent is owed, and when the last is spent someone calls one in)
Know Everybody (proficiency bonus doubled for Persuasion and Society checks)

Read the Room (after a minute of conversation, Insight contested by the person's Deception: on a success he learns one of their goals, one of their fears, or whether one thing they said was a lie, and who in the room they fear most)

Family Name (Society Heir background: the Ainsworth name gets him invitations, a table at any good restaurant and an audience with most of the city's rich, who assume he is one of them; the Ainsworths cut him off in 1939 and nobody at those tables knows he is broke)

personality.traits: I say the most outrageous thing in any room in the most charming voice. I know everybody's first name and their mother's maiden name. I tip too much with money I don't have.
personality.ideals: Everyone in this town is selling something. I simply tell them what it's worth.
personality.bonds: My clients, who are mostly young, mostly broke and mostly better than the pictures they're in. Vivian Lark is the best of them, and I sent her to the Sirocco because Harlan Shay asked me to.
personality.flaws: I owe Royce Ambler three thousand dollars at cards, I cannot stop playing, and Ambler has offered to forget all of it if I find out what Vivian has.

appearance: Thirty-four, slender, beautifully barbered, with a fine profile going slightly soft, pale blue eyes that have been drinking since lunch and miss nothing, and a dinner jacket worn as if it were pyjamas. A voice like a well-made cocktail.
backstory: Percival Ainsworth was the younger son of a Pasadena orange-and-railroad family, sent to Princeton, sent down from Princeton, sent to Paris, sent home, and cut off in 1939 after a scandal involving a Santa Anita racehorse and a borrowed Rolls-Royce. He became an agent because it was the only job he could get on charm alone. He represents twenty actors, mostly contract players, and Vivian Lark is the client he believes in. He knows her real name and where she comes from, he knows her bank, and he knows something he has told no one: Royce Ambler has telephoned him three times since the thirteenth, very friendly, asking whether Vivian 'has anything of mine', and offering to tear up Percy's markers if he finds out. He has not said yes. He has not said no. And Lyle Preston of the committee has asked him to lunch on Friday to talk about his clients' politics.
